figures.title: Figure 2.1. A cross-section of a foreland basin system. The Fort Worth Basin is considered as a foredeep basin within a foreland basin system (Modified from DeCelles and Giles, 1996).; Figure 2.2. Regional paleogeography of the southern mid-continent region during the Late Mississippian (325 Ma) showing the approximate position of the Fort Worth Basin close to the Island Chain resulted from the convergent collision between Laurussia and Gondwana. Llano Uplift and the Arch equator are shown. They played important rule in the evaluation of the Fort Worth Basin (Burner et al., 2011).
figures.shows: Top figure is a generalized cross-section illustrating the components of a foreland basin system and locating the Fort Worth Basin as a foredeep; bottom figure is a paleogeographic reconstruction of the southern mid-continent during the Late Mississippian showing the basin's position relative to major tectonic elements like the Llano Uplift, Transcontinental Arch, and Island Chain.

figures.title: Figure 2.8. Stratigraphic nomenclature used to define the Bend Conglomerate genetic sequences in the Boonsville field. figures.title: Figure 2.9. Composite genetic sequence illustrating the key chronostratigraphic surfaces and typical facies successions.
